4) Cross-region failover semantics: acceptable for compute to move (warm standby) vs. requirement to avoid any cross-border data copies at rest?
5) Backups & snapshots: acceptable recovery point objectives and whether backups must be geo-anchored in the same territory.

- We provide a targeted one-pager describing: hosted vs. dedicated vs. private options for geo-anchoring + a sample SLA/profile for log retention.

Alex — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick answers from our side to unblock the mapping exercise:

- PII scope: confirmed — name, DOB, MRN, SSN, raw clinician notes (free text) are treated as PHI. We will mark derived tokens/embeddings as low-sensitivity if stripped of identifiers.
- Retention: we need flexibility: short (30d) for general logs, 1 year for clinical audit trails, 7 years for regulatory hold when triggered.
- Log access: only security ops and a named list of SREs should see raw request payloads; data science should receive redacted logs or synthetic samples.
- Cross-region: for pilot we can accept compute failover to US from EU for transient availability, but any persisted storage for EU users must remain in EU.
- Backups: require backup snapshots encrypted and replicated only to EU if the tenant opts into EU residency.

I'll annotate the matrix and return by EOD Monday. Happy to do the security sync Wed 10am ET with your team.

Thanks — added a few technical clarifications below that we can paste into the one-pager appendix.

1) Requests vs. logs vs. cache:
- Requests (raw payloads): by default kept in ephemeral runtime memory and in short-term request logs (configurable to 0/30/90 days). For Hosted customers the default is 30 days; for Dedicated we can reduce to 0–7 depending on retention policy in the reserved environment.
- Inference logs (token-level traces): kept separately and can be redacted at ingest. We support field-level scrubbing rules (regex-based) and automated identifier removal for known PHI patterns.
- KV cache snapshots: checkpoints are created for warm start; snapshots are encrypted at rest and can be configured to be written only to region-anchored object storage when the tenant selects 'hard-anchor'. Snapshots are incremental and have separate retention controls.

2) Backups & replication:
- Backup snapshots are encrypted with tenant keys when BYOK is enabled. For geo-anchored tenants, replication targets are limited to the selected territory; cross-region replication will not be performed unless explicitly enabled with a signed change request.
- RPO/RTO: default RPO is 4 hours for model checkpoints; we can offer 1 hour RPO for Dedicated with appropriate capacity commits. RTO targets depend on the chosen failover policy and pre-warmed pools.

3) Cross-region failover semantics:
- Soft failover: routing shifts to a warm standby pool in another region; ephemeral runtime state (KV cache) is rehydrated from region-anchored snapshots where permitted. This implies transient cross-region data transfer for cache rehydration unless hard-anchor is selected.
- Hard-anchor mode: compute failover only within the same territory; if a territory-limited outage occurs and there is no local capacity, the system can either (a) return errors, or (b) route to a fallback model variant that uses masked inputs (no raw payload persisted).

4) Access controls & audit evidence:
- Full audit trails exist for admin operations and access to logs; we can provide a SOC 2 artifact bundle and a sample access log for review.
